open_risks: Own-words skills (ADR-011) are matched by simple keywords and are not reviewed; a provider can describe a lawful skill vaguely or misleadingly. The restricted-intent policy and listed-skill rule guard them, but popular labels should be reviewed and promoted into skills.yaml through vocabulary_gaps.

Scope is open to any lawful service and any public place; the restricted-intent policy is now the only refusal path. It is rule-based, has 46 labelled vectors plus backend tests, and has not been red-teamed by a second person (Person Two P2.S11).
Skill vocabulary is 115 tags; matching quality is untested at low provider density, and place questions have no human answerers until Phase 4, so they end Unknown.
Provider rate-limit budget is shared with the request read budget per caller address (60/min, in-process memory).
September 23 verification was local, on an isolated real PostgreSQL database: see docs/testing/phase-1-hardening-2026-09-23.md. G1 still needs joint staging evidence under ADR-004.

The Phase 1 rate limits are counted in one process's memory (FixedWindowLimiter). That is correct for a single instance and wrong the moment there are two, and it also means the limits survive across test runs — a second walkthrough inside fifteen minutes is refused. Wire Redis in before the backend is ever run as more than one process.

The missing launch-screen declaration caused a 320x480 compatibility window. Fixed and captured at full size on September 23. Largest-text controls are scrollable; physical-device visual/VoiceOver review remains pending.
UI tests now use the dedicated PlugUI scheme and require a running identity backend. Both text-size tests passed. They capture 7 states per size, not the full physical-device matrix.

PLUG's own access and refresh tokens are opaque and resolved against the sessions table on every request (ADR-006). That is one indexed read and one last_used_at write per authenticated call. It has not been load-tested; measure before assuming it holds.

Twilio outbound OTP is optionally implemented in Phase 1 under amended ADR-007, but no configured sender or real received-SMS evidence has been established. Development codes remain local-only; disabled delivery returns 503. Two-way SMS/iMessage remain later-phase work.

The connected iPhone is available, but Xcode provisioning refresh failed: the configured Personal development team does not support Sign in with Apple. Use an Apple Developer Program team that supports this capability, select it in Signing & Capabilities, enable the capability for the App ID, and refresh provisioning. Then follow the physical-device runbook. A signed Google-capable app was previously tested; that does not establish Apple capability.

PLUG_IDENTITY_PEPPER is required by the db and staging profiles, including for local ./dev databaseTest runs. It keys the stored phone, Apple-subject and one-time-code hashes, so rotating it makes every existing identity unrecognisable. It has no secret-storage home yet beyond .env.local and the CI workflow.

No account type in Phase 1 can be granted the admin scope, so every route under /v1/admin is refused — confirmed in the walkthrough. AdminStepUpAuthorization is in place ahead of the first admin route, but nothing exercises the allow path until Phase 5.

Terms, Privacy, and Support web routes now exist. Terms and Privacy explicitly await approved legal text; PLUG_WEB_URL must point at a reachable site on a real phone. Do not treat the development consent version as an approved published agreement.

Operational health routes reject requests carrying tunnel/proxy forwarding headers by design (SecurityConfiguration.directProbeOnly()). Confirmed from Person One's Mac/iPhone and, on 2026-09-22, Person Two's own Windows PC.
AWS staging is deferred (ADR-004) — no budget right now. Revisit no later than Phase 3, when Twilio needs a stable webhook URL a Quick Tunnel cannot provide.
